content_payload.front_text: y at end of 2+ syllable word = /iː/

slides.teacher_cue: y has a third sound. At the end of a word with two or more syllables, y makes long /iː/: happy, funny, baby, city, party, story. This connects to what you already know: y at the start of a word = /j/ (yes), y at the end of a one-syllable word = /aɪ/ (my, fly), y at the end of a multi-syllable word = /iː/ (happy, party). Three sounds, one letter — position and syllable count are the guide.
slides.expected_response: Students apply the three y rules and produce /iː/ correctly in multi-syllable words ending in y.
slides.correction_move: Review the three y rules side by side. Sort words: yes (y=/j/), my/fly (y=/aɪ/), happy/party (y=/iː/). Establish the syllable-count rule for the third sound.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /aɪ/ substitution in multi-syllable y words — Korean learners who learned y=/aɪ/ may generalise.

slides.slide_title: Choose the word where final y says /iː/

content_payload.correction_routine: At the end of a multi-syllable word, y says /iː/. At the end of a one-syllable word like my, y says /aɪ/.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both words. Students choose the word where final y says /iː/ and explain how syllable count helps.
slides.expected_response: Students identify happy as the /iː/ word and reject my as the /aɪ/ word.
slides.correction_move: Clap the syllables, then sort the pair by y sound.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students who know the sound but do not yet use syllable count as the cue.

slides.slide_title: Choose the word where final y says /iː/

content_payload.correction_routine: city ends with /iː/ because it has more than one syllable; fly ends with /aɪ/.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both words. Ask students to choose the /iː/ word and justify using the y rule.
slides.expected_response: Students identify city as the /iː/ word and explain why fly is different.
slides.correction_move: Clap syllables, then compare the two final y sounds aloud.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can shift from one-syllable y knowledge to the new multi-syllable rule.

slides.teacher_cue: Say happy — two syllables, y at end = /iː/. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say happy orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model happy orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /iː/ at end — not /aɪ/.
